newsitem.title: ITALY: Two Italians kidnapped in Yemen are released.
newsitem.headline: Two Italians kidnapped in Yemen are released.

text.p: Two Italians kidnapped by Yemeni tribesmen were released on Sunday, an official at the Italian embassy in the Yemeni capital Sanaa said.
Roberto Vesperini, an embassy official, confirmed the release in a live telephone interview with Italian state television RAI.
He said the two, Luigi Archetti and Maria Paola Mariconi, were first taken to the residence of the governor of the Yemeni capital and then to the interior ministry.
Vesperini said he had spoken by telephone to one of the two Italians, who had been held for a day, and was told both were in good condition.

Archetti and Mariconi were kidnapped on Saturday together with their Yemeni driver and a tour guide, who is also believed to be Yemeni, by the al-Yemenia al-Ulia tribe, tribal sources in Yemen told Reuters.
The kidnapping was the latest in a string of abductions in the poor state at the south end of the Arabian peninsula.
They were abducted in Kholan, about 60 km (40 miles) east of Sanaa, as part of a property dispute with the authorities, the security source in Yemen said.
Kidnapping is a common ploy by tribesmen holding grievances against the government or foreign oil firms operating in Yemen, one of the Arab world's most impoverished countries.
Tribesmen have tried to use hostages, who have included a U.S. diplomat and a Saudi ambassador, as bargaining chips in mostly land and water disputes.
In March four German tourists were kidnapped. Earlier that month a group of seven German tourists on a motorcycle tour in Yemen were also kidnapped.
In February a U.S. oil engineer was taken hostage by a Yemeni mountain tribe.
All hostages have been released unharmed so far.
